items.title: The sources
items.body:
| # | source | read by | governs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | `csi-spl-orc/src/bash/features/spool-install/assets/claude/claude-md/*.md` | every Claude seat on every box: spool-install (step y4) renders these parts into the installed global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; every mistral (vibe) seat: step y8 renders the same parts into `~/.vibe/AGENTS.md` (vibe loads AGENTS.md, never CLAUDE.md) | `05` seats run as the agent user; `07` permission mode bypass only; `10` push trunk, deploy dev and prd; `20` spawn an agent: launcher choice, the agent ceiling + count command, the data rule, the language rule; `25` stay in your own lane; `27` every lane carries an issue, keeps it and the docs current; `30` a cross-lane finding states version, tree and n |
| 1.2 | repo `CLAUDE.md` (the repo `AGENTS.md` only points to it, for vibe) | every agent working in this repo | repo rules: environments, service accounts only, nothing ad hoc, terraform via tf-runner, cheap gates before a push, version minting, the commit identity; pointers to 1.1 and to this page |
| 1.3 | `csi-spl-doc/doc/md/SPEC-spool-fleet-roles.md` | orchestrator and dispatcher seats | roles `001`..`003`, where messages come from, the routing rule, the leases, failover, hourly rotation |
| 1.4 | `csi-spl-doc/doc/md/lane-integration-rules.md` | a lane, when a rule of its seed seems odd | the why of the spawn seed's INTEGRATION (1)-(8), SCOPE (a)-(d) and DEPLOY-GATE (a)-(e); the rules themselves are in `spawn-agents/scripts/spawn-core.inc.sh` (`_spawn_seed_blocks`) |
| 1.5 | `csi-spl-orc/src/bash/features/spawn-agents/assets/commands/spawn-an-agent.md` + cnf `env.box.agent_split` (`csi-spl-cnf/csi-spl/all.env.yaml`) + `do_spl_lane_mix` | a seat that spawns | which vendor takes a task: the split (approximate, +/- tolerance over the last spawns), the kinds `spec`, `i18n`, `secret`, `hard` |
| 1.6 | `csi-spl-orc/src/bash/features/spawn-agents/assets/commands/{claude,grok,agy,qwen,mistral}-spawn.md` | a seat that runs that launcher | how to spawn or message one vendor's lane: count, brief, window, seed |
| 1.7 | `csi-spl-doc/doc/help/how-to-post.md` | everyone who posts in the spool | the one rule for a post: markdown, no fence; an attached file keeps its real extension (rule 13) |
| 1.8 | `csi-spl-doc/doc/md/developer-guide.md` | every coder, human or agent | explains the trunk strategy (rebase, push to master, CI deploys dev and prd, minted versions) and the never-force-push rule with what enforces it; homes no rule, points to each home |
| 1.9 | `csi-spl-doc/doc/md/workspace-rules.md` | a dispatcher writing a brief for a workspace's lane, and that lane | rules the owner set for one workspace, one section per workspace id (`ws-b`: every doc in English and Bulgarian) |
| 1.10 | `csi-spl-doc/doc/md/guides/devops-guide.md` | operator / DevOps | the GCP estate and the pipelines, test runs in production (the opt-in rule) |
| 1.11 | `csi-spl-doc/doc/md/rounds-rulebook.md` | planners, reviewers, dispatchers, row lanes | rules for creating bug-fix and refactoring rounds (at most 10 items, pushes per item, standing rules R1-R16) |

items.title: One home per rule
items.body:
| rule | its home | pointers elsewhere |
|---|---|---|
| agent ceiling (40) and the window-count command | 1.1 `20-spawn-an-agent.md` | repo `CLAUDE.md` (one line); each launcher 1.6 keeps the count command in its section 1.1, because a launcher is read on its own: the drift check (section 3) pins those copies to the home |
| agent-id grammar `^[acgmq]-[0-9]{3}$` | spec 061 section 0; in code `SPOOL_AGENT_ID_NEW_RX` (`spawn-agents/lib/spool-env.inc.sh`) | repo `CLAUDE.md` (link), 1.3 section 1 |
| data rule: personal data and secrets to claude, grok or mistral only, never qwen or agy | 1.1 `20-spawn-an-agent.md` | repo `CLAUDE.md` (one line); the routing row in 1.5 |
| language rule: agy has the final word on multilingual text | 1.1 `20-spawn-an-agent.md` | repo `CLAUDE.md` (one line); the `i18n` row in 1.5 |
| commit identity, no AI trailers | repo `CLAUDE.md`, the "Commits:" line (the canonical address the seed's LEAK-GATE defers to) | 1.4 section 5 (the why) |
| spool posts are markdown | 1.7 | repo `CLAUDE.md` (one line) |
| tangent discussions: a side issue (pop-up) in a topic gets its own discussion, links back, and gets its own issue if it is work (owner, HUM-10 t1 4f98d07c msgs 3e5d2bb1, 33ad90a1, fc6edfdb) | 1.7 section 8 | `runbook-dispatcher.md` section 3 (one line) |
| stay in your own lane („Всяка жаба да си знае гьола“): your brief only, a finding outside it to the orchestrator | 1.1 `25-stay-in-your-lane.md` | rendered, not copied, into every vendor's file: claude `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (y4; grok reads it through its default `compat.claude` scan), mistral `~/.vibe/AGENTS.md` (y8), agy `~/.gemini/config/rules/25-stay-in-your-lane.md` and qwen `~/.qwen/QWEN.md`, which is also qwen's memory file (y9); the mistral seed (`spawn-mistral.sh`, `spawn_rename_how`, one line), because vibe 2.26.0 keeps no memory file across sessions |
| every lane carries an issue (`wip` at placement, the key in every commit subject, an end reason when it does not land) and lands its doc change or a `Docs: none (<why>)` line (owner, HUM-10 t1 5ea2e615 msgs 5b6f2aa7, 5c4c410e, 346238a8) | 1.1 `27-lane-issue-and-docs.md` | the seed's `YOUR ISSUE` block (`_spawn_issue_block` in `spawn-core.inc.sh`); how it is enforced: `lane-issue-and-docs.md` |
| lane integration (commit, rebase, push, teardown) | the seed, `spawn-core.inc.sh` | 1.4 (the why) |
| a lane pushes master with `do_spl_push_master` in the background and polls `PUSH_CMD=status`; never a foreground `git push` nor a foreground loop around one (SPL-1578: the 15-min one-call cap killed 3 lanes on the push) | the seed's INTEGRATION (4), `spawn-core.inc.sh` | 1.4 section 3.3 (the why, the measurement) |
| never force-push master (`--force`, `--force-with-lease`, `+ref`, nor `SPL_PREPUSH_OVERRIDE`) without the owner's explicit approval of that one push, which the owner may do by hand; a refused push is fetch, rebase, re-test, push again (owner, HUM-10 2026-10-10 msgs 853a4084, 1cdfa5ba, 097f9de3, 1ca01c83, 3e095a04: every agent type) | the seed, `NO_FORCE` in `spawn-core.inc.sh` (`_spawn_seed_blocks`), rendered into every kind's seed: c-, g-, a-, q-, m- (guard: `spawn-agents/tests/test-seed-no-force-push.sh`, with a control per kind) | 1.4 section 3.2 (the why); the seed's INTEGRATION (4) points to it |
| ws-b: every doc is `<name>.en.md` (default) AND `<name>.bg.md`, agy writes the Bulgarian (owner, HUM-10 ws-b eb7f4883, msg c3ae5158) | 1.9 section 1.1 | `runbook-dispatcher.md` section 6 step 4 (one line: copy the workspace's section into the brief) |
| creating bug-fix and refactoring rounds: at most 10 items, push caps (aim 1, max 5), continuous execution with no owner go, standing rules R1-R16 (owner, HUM-10 msgs f477d3ea, 9b8fe16f, 2f994cf6, 0c3c223e, 3d22fcea) | 1.11 | 1.3 section 1.2, `SPEC-spool-project-refactor.md`, round plans `refactor-round-<N>-plan.md` |
| the dispatcher and orchestrator runbooks are qto docs (t1, System documentation / Runbooks); `runbook-dispatcher.md` and `runbook-orchestrator.md` are only their export: edit the qto doc, then `cd csi-spl-orc && ./run -a do_spl_doctree_export_md` (owner, HUM-10 t1 ee1e58d5, msg 0512415c) | the qto docs, mapped to their md paths in `csi-spl-doc/doc/md/qto-docs.tsv` | each md file's "generated from qto doc" line |
| tests do not run in prd by default; prd has an opt-in way to run any or all of them, operator picks which tests (owner, HUM-10 t1 cd592c84 msgs 4dfc19b5, 05d5d1b6) | 1.10 section 16 | none (the DevOps guide is its home) |
| spawn queue: work classes and bands (SPL-1817). Owner, HUM-10 t1 3209f8b8: msg a25bfdd6 ("refactoring ... the majority of the resources, then bug fixing, and only after that, new feature additions"), msg 36ee9cec ("at least 20% to 30% ... only dedicated to refactoring"), then the binding one, msg 8cb6cc7d ("20% to 30% refactoring, 20% to 30% bug fixing ... the rest will be new feature implementation ... a bypass lane for a new feature ... I will have to do that explicitly. You have to keep track for me"), and msg ad816f96 (orchestrator, dispatcher and GC must know it). **The rule:** every queued spawn request has a class, `ci` (a CI-red fix on trunk, counts as bug), `refactor`, `bug` or `feature`, never guessed (`SPAWN_CLASS`, required). Bands of the live lanes with a class: refactor 20-30%, bug 20-30%, feature the rest. The placer takes a `ci` row first, then a flagged one, then the class furthest under its band; a class over its band only when no other class waits; ties refactor > bug > feature, then time in line. `SPAWN_URGENT=1`: a bug (owner-reported prd breakage) placed over its band, the dispatcher's call. `SPAWN_BYPASS=<owner msg id>`: a feature outside the bands, ONLY on the owner's explicit ask, recorded on the hub row and in the orch box's bypass log. Refactor or bug under 20% with nothing of it queued: the placer sends the dispatch holder one blocker an hour. The report for the owner: `./run -a do_spl_spawn_share` (live lanes by class, %, verdict, lanes with no class, the bypasses); the dispatcher posts it | this row; in code `SPL_SPAWN_BANDS` (`csi-spl-orc/src/bash/run/spl-spawn-share.func.sh`), the class order `askClassRank` (`csi-spl-api/.../store/fleet_ask.go`), rdb `0195_fleet_asks_class.sql`; tests `spl-spawn-queue.tst.sh` section 10, `TestFleetAskQueueClassOrder` | 1.3 section 4.3 (one paragraph); `runbook-orchestrator.md`, `runbook-dispatcher.md`, `gc-agent.md` section 2.4 and `gc-prompt.md` step 3 (pointers) |
| idle filler: spare capacity becomes lanes from open issues (SPL-1922). Owner, HUM-10 t1 71dbbf15, poll 41155726, answer msg 3c91b4c1: "(A) Yes, from open issues (bugs and features), within the share bands". **The rule:** when the box pick (`do_spl_box_pick`) says a box is below its LOW mark and the spawn queue has 0 queued and 0 placing, `do_spl_spawn_fill` queues the next open issues (status todo, then eval; priority 1 first; oldest first) of kind issue labelled `bug` or `feature` (the label is the class, never guessed), the class furthest under its band first and never a class over its band. Skipped: labels `needs-owner`, `blocker`, `epic`; a human assignee; an issue a live lane or an ask (open, queued or closed this week) already holds. How many: enough lanes to bring the box to its low mark, one lane counted as one core (`SPAWN_FILL_CORES_PER_LANE`), at most `SPAWN_FILL_MAX` (default 1) a tick. The vendor: `do_spl_lane_mix`, kind `complex_coding`; an issue that names a secret asks it sensitive and goes only to claude, grok or mistral. It never spawns: it writes the brief (`Issue:` + `Class:`), puts the ask and enqueues it with `do_spl_spawn_enqueue`; the placer places. Dry run by default; the switch `SPAWN_FILL=on` or cnf `env.box.spawn_fill.enabled: true`, absent = off; the orchestrator installs the cron (`do_spl_spawn_fill_install_cron`) and turns it on | this row; in code `csi-spl-orc/src/bash/run/spl-spawn-fill.func.sh`, test `spl-spawn-fill.tst.sh` | `runbook-orchestrator.md` section 5.1 (pointer) |
| the orchestrator never runs terraform jobs (plan, apply, reconcile) itself: spawn a lane to run them and report back (owner, HUM-10 t1 cd592c84, msg 116ab2b5) | 1.3 section 1.4 | the orchestrator rotation brief (`spl-orch-rotate.func.sh`) |

items.title: The drift check
items.body:
`cd csi-spl-orc && ./run -a do_check_fleet_rules_drift` reads the sources in
section 1 and fails when two of them disagree on a pinned fact:

| # | fact | compared |
|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | id-letters | every `[..]-[0-9]{3}` letter class in the sources vs `SPOOL_AGENT_ID_NEW_RX` |
| 3.2 | ceiling-count | the window-count regex in 1.1 `20` vs every launcher and any other source |
| 3.3 | ceiling-number | the default of `install.sh` and `y4-claude-config.sh` vs "Agent ceiling: N" in the repo `CLAUDE.md` |
| 3.4 | data-rule | every `fleet-pin data-rule-vendors` pin (1.1 `20`, 1.5) agrees, its prose names each pinned vendor, and `do_spl_lane_mix`'s secret pick is in the set |
| 3.5 | language-rule | the same for the `fleet-pin language-rule-final` pins and `do_spl_lane_mix`'s `i18n` pick |
| 3.6 | commit-address | the repo `CLAUDE.md` "Commits:" address vs every recent commit by that author name |

It runs in the pre-push hygiene part (`do_check_pre_push`) and in the orc
suite (`csi-spl-orc/src/bash/tests/check-fleet-rules-drift.tst.sh`, with a
control per fact that plants a disagreement). `FLEET_RULES_HOME=<home>` adds a
box's INSTALLED copies (`<home>/.claude/CLAUDE.md`,
`<home>/.claude/commands/*-spawn.md`), which refresh only on a spool-install
run.

A changed rule: edit its home, then any pinned copy, then run the check.
